channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Yen Is Vulnerable With Japan on Holiday After BOJ Disappoints
item.description: The yen is vulnerable to sharp moves and further declines over the next week, with a three-day holiday in Japan set to reduce trading liquidity and investors disappointed that the central bank didn’t offer stronger guidance on the pace of future interest rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Hideyuki Sano and Umesh Desai

item.title: Hong Kong’s Chan Says City to Expand Market for Dim Sum Bonds
item.description: Hong Kong plans to expand the Dim Sum bond market and develop the yuan-denominated gold and commodity markets to further enhance the city’s financial role and pricing power, Financial Secretary Paul Chan wrote in his weekly blog Sunday.
item.dc:creator: K. Oanh Ha

item.title: Heavy Rain Disrupts Trains in Japan as Tropical Storm Approaches
item.description: The approaching tropical cyclone Dujuan could cause suspensions and delays on train lines in the greater Tokyo area, with possible disruptions from as early as Sunday evening through Tuesday morning, major operator East Japan Railway Co. warned.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Maekawa

item.title: Australia Home Auction Clearance Rates Fall Amid Rate Hike Fears
item.description: Australia’s residential real estate market remained subdued with auction clearance rates falling this week as concerns the central bank will increase interest rates later this month grow, according to property researcher Cotality.
item.dc:creator: Edward Johnson

item.title: Venezuela, TotalEnergies Pave Way for Oil Company’s Return
item.description: Venezuela and TotalEnergies SE signed a memorandum of understanding on Saturday, setting up the French company for a return to operations in the South American country.
item.dc:creator: Jose Orozco and Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: Trump Reignites Kennedy Center Fight
item.description: President Donald Trump’s plans for the Kennedy Center are hitting legal roadblocks as questions mount over the landmark’s future. Bloomberg’s Shaquille Omari breaks down the escalating battle over one of Washington’s most iconic cultural institutions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Turkey Detains Top Finance Executives in Funds Scheme, NTV Says
item.description: Turkish authorities on Saturday detained high-profile finance executives as part of an investigation into a “ponzi-like” funds scheme.
item.dc:creator: Beril Akman

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/19/2026
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Brookings Institution VP and Director of Foreign Policy Program Suzanne Maloney, Signum Global Advisors Senior Partner & Fmr. US Embassy London Deputy Chief of Mission Lew Lukens, Merrill Head of CIO Market Strategy & BofA Private Bank Joe Quinlan, Vanity Fair Contributing Writer Chris Whipple, Utah Gov. & “Off Ramp” Author Spencer Cox and NYC Dept. of Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Immersive movie screening, the plea for headphones, all-you-can-drink German method coming to the US, and old rock stars still rocking: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini as they go over interesting headlines from this week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New York Builds Data Team to Target Consumer Ripoffs
item.description: New York City is building a 36-person bureau of data scientists, technologists and economists to analyze company records for potential violations involving pricing, wages and other consumer and worker protections. NYC Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that the effort is designed to give the city the technical expertise to enforce existing laws as algorithms and AI play a growing role in how companies set prices and compensation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Governor Cox Says Americans Need Healthier Conflict
item.description: Utah Governor Spencer Cox joins Bloomberg This Weekend and argues Americans need more substantive disagreement without the contempt he says is fueling polarization, damaged relationships and political violence. In his new book, Off Ramp, Cox calls for healthier political conflict and stronger local connections while also arguing that policymakers need more expertise to address emerging challenges such as AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hormuz Oil Shipments Hit Six-Month High, US Commander Says
item.description: Oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz in the past two weeks reached the highest level in six months, signaling that US naval protection and mine clearance efforts are “paying off,” a regional US commander said.
item.dc:creator: Tony Czuczka

item.title: SpaceX’s Nasdaq 100 Weight Is Confirmed at 2.82% in Rebalance
item.description: SpaceX will make up 2.82% of the Nasdaq 100 when the index’s quarterly rebalance takes effect Monday, according to data obtained by Bloomberg, locking in a sharp increase from its current weighting of about 1.28%.
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Lee

item.title: Companies Avoid Selling the Bonds Investors Crave: Credit Weekly
item.description: Investors are clamoring for the kind of debt companies are reluctant to sell now: longer-term bonds.
item.dc:creator: Emily Graffeo, Caleb Mutua, Finbarr Flynn and Ronan Martin

item.title: Diesel Prices Keep Pressure on Fed and Markets
item.description: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers confront inflation that remains above target and uncertainty tied to geopolitical developments. Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mozambique Cut by Moody’s on Heightened Restructuring Risks
item.description: Moody’s Ratings cut its assessment of Mozambique’s creditworthiness deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill

item.title: US Greenland Deal Shifts Focus to Investment
item.description: A new security agreement between the US, Denmark and Greenland would expand the American military role while preserving Greenlandic sovereignty, shifting attention toward potential US investment in mining, infrastructure and tourism. Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that Greenland welcomes investment but faces formidable obstacles including limited transportation infrastructure, a small workforce and the high cost of developing projects in the Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UN Talks Offer a New Opening on Iran War
item.description: World leaders head to the UN General Assembly as Gulf states seek renewed diplomacy to reduce attacks, restore more predictable energy flows and move the Iran war away from active conflict. Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and other regional infrastructure are adding urgency to those efforts as Gulf economies face mounting pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Arabia Billionaires’ Family Office Dubai Bet Adds to London Exodus
item.description: An investment firm for one of Saudi Arabia’s richest families is relocating from London to Dubai, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest example of private wealth outflows from the UK to the Gulf despite heightened uncertainty from the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Dinesh Nair and Ben Stupples
